harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured a 1 GiB file-backed LUKS2 encrypted XFS volume mounted at /srv/secure. It unlocks and mounts automatically through systemd using /etc/crypttab and /etc/fstab. The RHEL 10.0 release and kernel remain unchanged, SELinux remains enforcing, SSH remains available, and no failed units remain. Reboot persistence was verified with a changed boot identity and preserved data checksum.
actions_performed: Installed the signed RHEL cryptsetup 2.8.1 package.
Generated a node-local root-only unlock key.
Created the LUKS2 encrypted backing volume and XFS filesystem.
Configured native systemd boot-time unlocking and mounting.
Verified incorrect-key rejection and absence of plaintext data in the encrypted backing file.
Rebooted node1 safely and verified automatic recovery, data integrity, write access, administrative access, and cleanup.

evidence.summary: Shows the active AES-XTS LUKS2 mapping, XFS filesystem mounted at /srv/secure, restricted permissions, incorrect-key rejection, and absence of the plaintext marker from the backing file.

evidence.requirement: Automatic unlock and mount at boot
evidence.summary: Shows crypttab/fstab integration, a successful systemd-managed unlock/remount cycle, and active cryptsetup and mount units sourced from those files after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel preserved
evidence.summary: Before and after evidence shows RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 unchanged.

Healthy baseline used boot ID 254597f8-4ac9-4062-8be8-44eba1f6d2e9; the safe reboot was acknowledged; boot ID changed to 01435e0b-87e3-4b78-aa14-cbb90e77e399; afterward SSH, cryptsetup, and the mount were active, the protected-data checksum matched, and read/write behavior succeeded.

evidence.requirement: Final security, cleanup, and system health
evidence.summary: Confirms root-only key/container permissions, SELinux labels, removal of temporary test artifacts, active SSH and storage units, valid filesystem configuration, and zero failed systemd units.
